notes.title: Made in Brazil Sale 2024
notes.notes:
The [b]Made in Brazil[/b] Sale is currently going on Steam. It's the 2nd consecutive year in which the event takes place, celebrating games made by Brazilian Developers!

The [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/MadeinBrazilSale]Made in Brazil Sale[/url][/b] takes place between the 14th and 19th of February and has more than 500 Brazilian titles!

The sale has games already published, new releases and even titles that are yet to be released, such as [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2125110/Brazilian_Street_Food_Simulator/]Brazilian Street Food Simulator[/url]!

[h2]About the event[/h2]
Conceived by [b]Eduardo Lamhut[/b], developer of the company [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/43317964]Bitcake Studio[/url] from Rio de Janeiro, the action emerged after the mobilization of studios and teams from all regions of the country. A great demonstration of the growth and maturity of the national industry.

Unprecedented and officially approved by the platform, the campaign means highlighting Brazilian games in the most popular space: the Steam homepage, thus promoting consumption and the dissemination of titles.

notes.title: Sell sugar cane juice in the toilet? BR Food Sim Devlog #2
notes.notes:
Brazilian Street Food Simulator devlog 2 is out!

I talk about bugs and problems when using physics with Skeletal Meshes (both UE and Unity), my final engine choice, as well my sandbox plans, like mechanics such as [b]selling rat contaminated sugar cane juice in a toilet[/b].

NOTICE: Video in 🇧🇷  Portuguese, with English subtitles available.

[previewyoutube=dQXOgHAiCCE;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Sandbox Gameplay Preview in First Person with Physical interactions
notes.notes:
First gameplay preview: in Brazilian Street Food Simulator you have total freedom to assemble your street food store, stalls and food production. 

Brazilian 🇧🇷 vendors improvise and make a lot of contraptions, and you can do the same in the game. It's a simulator and tycoon like no other!

PS: initially the game was already being developed as a first person game, then I pivoted it and for some months the game was being developed as a top-down tycoon - I got to a point of a playable tycoon prototype. But I have now changed it back to the original design of it being a first person game where you control things directly, this aligns better with my original vision for the game.

PS 2: in the video, you can see the prototyping scene, which is why the environment is gray. Typically, scenes like this are called "asset zoo" or "gameplay playground", for you to test systems and assets (3D models, etc) during development. 🧑‍💻

[previewyoutube=03CDbHK5etE;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Making my Simulator Indie Game in 3 Engines - BR Food Sim Devlog 1
notes.notes:
Since the game was published in August last year, it went viral for a week and I started facing choice paralysis between the many game concepts AND game engines. I ended up making the game with three engines at the same time. And now I finally came to a point to take a stance and move things forward for good, with Brazilian Street Food Simulator!

[previewyoutube=MIdwLRzjw18;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Made in Brazil Sale
notes.notes:
The [b]Made in Brazil[/b] Sale is currently going on Steam. It's the first event of its kind on Steam, celebrating games made by Brazilian Developers (or with Brazilians in the team), while Brazil celebrates its worldwide known [b]Carnival[/b] event.

The [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42974040/sale/MadeinBrazilSale]Made in Brazil Sale[/url][/b] takes place between the 18th and 23rd of February and has more than 500 titles!

The sale has games already published, new releases and even titles that are yet to be released. 

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2125110/Brazilian_Street_Food_Simulator/]Brazilian Street Food Simulator[/url] is a highlight in the event, and I'm humbled to say that it is at the side of legendary indie games like Oniken, Celeste and others!

[h2]About the event[/h2]
Conceived by [b]Eduardo Lamhut[/b], developer of the company [url=https://store.steampowered.com/search/?publisher=BitCake+Studio&snr=2_groupannouncements_detail_]Bitcake Studio[/url] from Rio de Janeiro, the action emerged after the mobilization of studios and teams from all regions of the country. A great demonstration of the growth and maturity of the national industry.

Unprecedented and officially approved by the platform, the campaign means highlighting Brazilian games in the most popular space: the Steam homepage, thus promoting consumption and the dissemination of titles.

Source from the about section: the Brazilian developer [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/aocagamelab]Aoca Game Lab[/url].

notes.title: Brazilian Street Food Simulator Goes Viral In Brazil and is All Over the News
notes.notes:
Brazilian Street Food Simulator was announced publicly for the first time on 19/08/22, [url=https://twitter.com/PardallGames/status/1560658418431434753]with a Twitter post with the trailer[/url]. Just 12 hours later it reached more than 1 million impressions and more than 300,000 video views! The announcement video currently has 390K views.

A [url=https://clips.twitch.tv/ApatheticYawningArmadilloTF2John-g13i9vbg_P3mFjgV]streamer with 6 million followers[/url] quickly talked about the game and a big portal that [url=https://adrenaline.com.br/noticias/v/78093/caldo-de-cana-pastel-game-indie-brazilian-street-food-simulator]created an article[/url] about the game

After that, as of today, the game has been covered by the majority of Brazil's biggest tech and gaming websites, and by some big YouTube and Instagram accounts.

Notice that all of this happened organically, without paid advertisement and without any kind of prior contact!
